title: Worktree isolation: lease the path, not the claim; Items 2/3 already shipped
summary: start_task only sets overlay status — it never creates a worktree, so the lease belongs at the real contention point: createWorktree() in lib/git.js, which is where two parallel agents would both run `git worktree add` against the same path. Lease = sidecar <wt>.lease written atomically with O_EXCL ('wx'); second writer gets {contended,held}. Stale leases (dead pid + aged past ORCH_LEASE_STALE_MS=1h) are reclaimable; removeWorktree frees it. Dirty-GC guard goes INSIDE gcWorktree (re-probe `git status --porcelain` right before remove), not just in classification — classification is scan-time, the reap is confirm-time, so only an execution-time re-check closes the TOCTOU window. Items 2 (branch-per-task) and 3 (judged merge-queue) were left untouched: the existing orch/attempt/<slug> convention already gives each task its own branch off HEAD with a real merge diff, and merge_attempt→/git/merge→mergeBranch already auto-aborts on conflict for the judge to escalate. Renaming to darwin/task-<id> would break every in-flight worktree + the merge/GC paths that key off orch/attempt/* — pure churn against working code.
